reason: E1 directly supports the formation and mechanical benefits of coherent nanoprecipitates in tungsten-based HEAs, while E2 provides evidence that AM refractory HEAs are viable but face helium bubble challenges and that microstructural homogeneity matters. premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates in tungsten-based refractory HEAs can be induced by a stepwise controllable thermal process.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, enhancing ductility while maintaining strength.
Additively manufactured refractory HEAs can be produced with acceptable mechanical properties but suffer from helium bubble growth under irradiation.
Increasing compositional complexity in HEAs may increase tolerance to He irradiation, but microstructural homogeneity is critical for performance.
